nodes.label: Isolated Module Composition
nodes.rationale: Each capability is isolated in its own module or subsystem, with extension.js limited to construction and teardown, so concerns can evolve independently.

nodes.label: Owned Fullscreen State
nodes.rationale: Fullscreen exit triggers affect only windows fullscreened through Tessera, preventing new-window and Escape handling from interrupting application-owned video or game fullscreen.

nodes.label: Installed Source Reverification
nodes.rationale: Porting decisions should be checked against the target system's extracted gresource source and typelibs instead of relying on assumptions or generalized GNOME knowledge.

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Recomputation
nodes.rationale: Layout, launcher results, and panel reveal state are repeatedly re-derived from authoritative live state so missed events and stale intermediate state self-correct.

nodes.label: Clipboard History Privacy
nodes.rationale: Clipboard history is opt-in, excludes password-manager offers and locked sessions, and keeps clipboard contents out of general ranking history.

nodes.label: Non-Overlapping Match Tiers
nodes.rationale: Exact, prefix, word, acronym, substring, subsequence, and typo score bands do not overlap, preventing weak matches from outranking stronger kinds of match.

nodes.label: Open Windows Priority
nodes.rationale: Open windows receive first claim on result capacity and sort first because switching to existing user-visible content is the launcher's most common task.

nodes.label: Provider Controller UI Separation
nodes.rationale: Providers emit data without rendering, the UI draws ranked sections without searching, and the controller alone scores and orders results, making providers independently extensible.

nodes.label: Debounced Relayout Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Dirty workspaces accumulate into one idle flush so bursts of window and workspace events coalesce, while frame comparison makes geometry application converge without feedback loops.

nodes.label: Pure Integer Layout Geometry
nodes.rationale: Split geometry uses integer arithmetic and remainder assignment to avoid drift, overlap, and rounding gaps at any tree depth or fractional scale.

nodes.label: Reconciled Layout Tree
nodes.rationale: A binary split tree preserves focus-aware insertion and sibling-local space recovery, while reconciliation against live workspace membership prevents structural state from becoming stale.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Window Membership
nodes.rationale: Identity-level layout membership is separated from transient tileability so minimized or maximized windows retain their tree slots and return to the exact prior position.

nodes.label: Manual UI Verification
nodes.rationale: Panel, compositor, keybinding, and live actor behavior requires manual testing because GNOME Shell provides no supported headless harness for third-party extension UI.

nodes.label: Pure Logic Test Seam
nodes.rationale: Logic-dense layout, matching, and calculator code is isolated from GNOME imports so it can receive real unit tests outside the compositor.

nodes.label: Eval-Free Calculator Parser
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic uses a tokenizer and recursive-descent grammar rather than eval, rejecting every character and construct outside the supported expression language.

nodes.label: Cooperate with GNOME Public APIs
nodes.rationale: Workspace switching, window movement, and resizing use GNOME's public APIs so focus, animations, dynamic workspace lifetime, and floating rules remain GNOME-owned.

nodes.label: Captured Target Window
nodes.rationale: The popup captures focus when it opens because its modal grab makes live focus at activation time an unreliable representation of the user's original target.

nodes.label: Shell-Free Command Execution
nodes.rationale: Commands require an explicit prefix, are parsed into argv, and are spawned without an interpreter so shell separators and substitutions cannot execute.

nodes.label: GNOME-Owned Behavior Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: Tessera will not reimplement animations, focus rules, dynamic workspace lifetime, or floating decisions that GNOME already owns, especially where doing so would require monkey-patching internals.

nodes.label: Public GNOME Integration
nodes.rationale: Tessera brings a Hyprland-style workflow to GNOME through the same public Mutter and Shell APIs GNOME uses, preserving GNOME-owned behavior instead of replacing the compositor.

nodes.label: Explicit Inline Active Colors
nodes.rationale: Active colors are always concrete inline values applied before class changes so St transitions cannot sample and flash a stale default blue.

nodes.label: Per-Window Floating Membership Override
nodes.rationale: Floating is orthogonal per-window state injected into the pure membership filter, not a third workspace layout mode.

nodes.label: Persistent User Layout Choices
nodes.rationale: Stacked-workspace and floating-window sets live at module scope so user choices survive GNOME's lock-cycle disable and enable while transient trees and signals rebuild cleanly.

nodes.label: Blur Disabled by Default
nodes.rationale: Shell.BlurEffect paints the full rectangular allocation and cannot follow rounded corners, so disabling it preserves exact transparent corners and avoids the visible artifact.

nodes.label: Literal Launcher Theme Values
nodes.rationale: Runtime theme values are resolved to concrete inline colors and dimensions so St transitions cannot leak incorrect class-based colors.

nodes.label: Stacked Group Posture
nodes.rationale: Stacked mode requires at least two layout members and auto-exits below that count because a one-tab group is worse than a full-area tiled window.

nodes.label: Tab-Bar Visibility Ownership
nodes.rationale: Stack tab bars omit trackFullscreen because GNOME force-writes visibility for tracked chrome, conflicting with overview, gesture, maximize, and fullscreen visibility decisions owned by the tiling manager.

nodes.label: Workspace Chrome Layering
nodes.rationale: Tab bars are restacked directly above ordinary windows so panels, lock shields, overview UI, menus, and notifications naturally cover them.

nodes.label: trackFullscreen Visibility Ownership
nodes.rationale: GNOME force-assigns visible on trackFullscreen chrome, so actors with owner-controlled visibility must avoid that flag.

nodes.label: Defensive Private API Reach
nodes.rationale: The swipe-tracker private field is accessed through guards and exception handling so future incompatibility disables only optional gesture enhancements, never core correctness.

nodes.label: Absolute Swipe Progress Mapping
nodes.rationale: GNOME's swipe progress is an absolute fractional workspace index, so preview uses clamped round(progress), is verified against workspace-switched, and self-pauses only after repeated mismatches.

nodes.label: Exact Disable Restoration
nodes.rationale: disable() must leak no signals, actors, timers, or keybindings and must restore external schema values and shell state exactly.

nodes.label: Lazy Launcher Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: While disabled the launcher retains only settings watchers; enabling creates providers and UI, while disabling destroys providers, caches, timeouts, actors, and modal grabs.

nodes.label: Reversible Extension Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: All extension changes, including conflicting keybindings, are intended to be restored exactly when the extension is disabled.

nodes.label: Graph-First Codebase Navigation
nodes.rationale: Scoped graph queries, paths, explanations, and wiki navigation are preferred because they surface a much smaller relevant subgraph than raw reports or source searches.

nodes.label: Incremental Graph Currency
nodes.rationale: Running graphify update after code modifications keeps the project knowledge graph synchronized without API cost.

nodes.label: Keybinding Override Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Conflicting key values are saved exactly, cleared, watched and reasserted while active, then restored exactly, including Ubuntu Dock's independent grabs.

nodes.label: ES Module Reload Constraint
nodes.rationale: GNOME Shell caches imported ES modules for the process lifetime, so disabling and enabling an extension cannot reload changed JavaScript; X11 shell restart or Wayland logout is required.

nodes.label: Safe Install from Symlink Mode
nodes.rationale: The install script removes only the extension symlink before forced installation because the underlying GNOME installer recursively follows symlinks and can otherwise delete the repository.

nodes.label: Yaru Theme Accent Mapping
nodes.rationale: GNOME 46 on Ubuntu exposes no standalone accent-color key, so Tessera reads gtk-theme and maps extracted Yaru variant colors without writing the external schema.
